persona: Upset and talks fast, with asides. The watch was a reward to himself after finishing a trade qualification. Lost the original receipt, so the jeweller printed a copy two days after the accident. Sent one photo from his phone and does not know the file is damaged.
initial_message: I'm honestly gutted!! Sunday morning (the 13th) I was taking my watch off before a shower and it slipped out of my hand onto the bathroom tiles. The glass has cracked right across and one of the lugs is bent. I saved for ages for that watch. What do I need to do to claim?? I've got a photo and the receipt.

facts.incident.description: I was taking my watch off before a shower and it slipped out of my hand. It fell about a metre and landed face down on the tiled bathroom floor.
facts.incident.cause: Dropped by accident onto a tiled floor
facts.loss.description: The watch glass is cracked right across the face, the lug on the upper right is bent, and the second hand has come loose

contents.items.contents.item.description: Automatic wristwatch, 40 mm, steel case and bracelet, blue dial

facts.contents.receipt_availability: A reprint of the receipt from the jeweller, available now. I lost the original.
facts.policyholder.name: Jack Ironbark
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the watch on the bathroom tiles, taken on my phone on Sunday morning. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: Reprint of the receipt from Orchard Lane Jewellers, printed on 15 September 2026 because I lost the original. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_receipt_dates: I bought the watch on 18 October 2024. The shop printed this copy for me on 15 September, two days after I dropped it.

facts.if_asked_about_a_repair_quote: I have not taken it to a watchmaker yet.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo looking down at a steel wristwatch with a steel link bracelet lying face up on pale grey ceramic bathroom floor tiles. The glass over the plain dark blue dial is cracked in one jagged line right across the face, and the steel lug at the upper right is bent out of line. The dial has simple baton hour markers only. Soft morning daylight from a window, the corner of a white bath mat at the edge of the frame. Close-up of the watch only. No people, no text, no logos.

design.notes: Plan feature innocent_reprint_date_after_loss with condition corrupt_file. The reprint date (15 September 2026) is after the accident, the purchase date (18 October 2024) is not; only the purchase date counts (rules, section 3). The condition is applied to the photo, not the receipt, so the receipt dates stay readable and the check stays clear. On main a truncated JPEG is stored as an Evidence record with file_status failed and the message that the image could not be read, so E2 asserts the record exists; it does not satisfy the incident image requirement.

triage.rationale: Accidental damage to one watch (NZD 2,450) at the insured address, nobody hurt, receipt reprint supplied, policy on file. The only photo of the damage is truncated and cannot be opened, and the claimant can only send a new one later, so required material is unreadable and someone must follow it up. The receipt reprint date (15 September) is after the accident, but only the purchase date (18 October 2024) counts, so there is no indicator. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Purchase date 18 October 2024 is before the incident on 13 September 2026; the reprint date 15 September 2026 is ignored

quote_before_loss.basis: No quote or assessment in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 April 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2019-04-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.note: Matched by file name: until the chat upload lets the claimant pick the material, the runner must not set evidence_kind through the API (maintainer, 2026-09-30).

On main the truncated JPEG is accepted as image/jpeg, fails the decode check in backend/services/image_readiness.py and is kept with file_status failed (backend/services/evidence.py _settle_image), so the record exists but is not usable.

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that the loss is covered or will be paid, or that it is not.

The Agent treats the reprint date as a problem: calls it suspicious, asks for the original receipt because of it, or says it may affect the claim. A neutral request to confirm when the watch was bought is fine.

The Agent asks for a photo of the damaged watch that it can open (sent again, as another file, or later), or records that one will be sent later. It does not have to explain why the first file failed.
The Agent describes what the watch photo shows, or says the photo confirms the damage. The file cannot be opened; repeating what the claimant wrote is fine.

allowed_variation: Whether the Agent asks the claimant to confirm when the watch was bought
